scope: Synthetic qwen35moe fixtures (4 layers: 3 Gated DeltaNet, 1 gated full attention; 16 routed experts top-4 plus a shared expert), CPU only, cloud container (4-core Xeon, AVX-512, AMX). Random weights: these runs judge implementations against the model's definition, not model quality or speed.

binaries.gnostral_capture_engine: engine tree e68287e + patches 0001-0009 + Phase 3a kernels (feat/engine-program f4ac8e6), public candle reconstruction (BUILD-ONLY); plain mistral.rs qwen35moe path (residency refuses this architecture, F-027)
binaries.llama_cpp: b11857 (701fd25), CPU build, REPACK and AMX_INT8 available on this host
binaries.reference: harness/synthetic-moe/qwen35moe_reference.py, float64, from transformers 5.20.2 modeling_qwen3_5_moe.py and llama.cpp b11857 conversion/qwen.py; expert tensors dequantised with b11857 gguf-py

self_consistency.method: per engine, the decode-path token at step i versus one prefill of prompt plus the first i tokens, i < 6

judged_against_reference.method: teacher forcing on each engine's own tokens; the reference argmax at every step and the gap between the engine's top-2 logprobs and the reference's

engine_vs_llama_tokens.kquant: 3/32 prompts identical, 37% prefix agreement, first divergence at step 1 on 15 prompts

ablations_kquant_engine_vs_llama.note: token agreement on random weights is noisy and was not used for the verdict; kept because it pointed at the experts only after the reference existed

speed_note: not a benchmark: on these fixtures the engine decodes 20 tok/s (kquant) and 92 tok/s (f32), llama.cpp 1275 and 762 tok/s; engine runs show about as much system time as user time
